guidance: Write an initiative-level PRD or behavior-focused feature spec. PRD mode uses `<Subject> - Agile PRD`; Feature mode uses `<Subject> - Agile Feature Spec`. The document title is separate metadata; body headings begin at level 1 and do not exceed level 4. Keep the required core concise and omit unused optional sections. Give each rule and acceptance condition one authoritative home; reference it elsewhere instead of duplicating it. Use `? [NEEDS_INPUT]` for a material unresolved choice or fact, `* [PROPOSAL]` for unaccepted suggested behavior, and `! [HYPOTHESIS]` for a plausible explanation still under investigation. Never present a proposal or hypothesis as established behavior or a decision. Do not invent research, baselines, commitments, stakeholders, or quantitative measures. A success measure may be qualitative when that is the useful evidence.

outline.title: Context & Scope
outline.guidance: The required top-level context for the product or feature specification. Its required children establish the problem and outcome; requirements define included scope. Optional journeys and delivery considerations belong here only when useful.

children.title: Problem & Users
children.guidance: Describe the problem, affected users or systems, and relevant current behavior. Do not invent personas or claim facts without evidence.

children.title: Outcomes & Success Measures
children.guidance: State the intended outcome and how it could be observed. Distinguish an outcome from a measured baseline or existing telemetry. Propose a target only when useful and label it `* [PROPOSAL]`; do not imply new instrumentation is in scope. Do not repeat a separate success measure under every requirement.

children.title: Non-Goals
children.guidance: Optional collection of exclusions that materially clarify the boundary. Do not require IDs or detailed rationale for simple exclusions.

children.title: Excluded Capability or Scope: {exclusion}
children.guidance: State the exclusion and its useful boundary or rationale. Replace {exclusion} with a descriptive name for the exclusion; omit exclusions that add no clarity.

children.title: Requirements
children.guidance: The authoritative collection of included capabilities and constraints. Include functional and relevant quality requirements. Requirements define included scope; add a separate scope summary only when the boundary would otherwise be unclear.

children.title: Requirement: {summary}
children.guidance: Replace {summary} with a descriptive name for one coherent capability or constraint. Split independently valuable or deferrable capabilities, not every step or rule. A requirement need not use a user-story sentence or REQ-xxx identifier; add stable identifiers only when useful for reference or tracking.

children.title: Behavior & Rules
children.guidance: Describe the required behavior, triggers, actors, applicable conditions, state changes, observable outcomes, and relevant exceptions where they apply. Include design references and constraints where they explain this requirement. Keep each rule in one authoritative place.

children.title: Acceptance Criteria
children.guidance: State observable pass/fail conditions that verify the behavior, including relevant edge cases. Use Given / When / Then for interactions, transitions, or flows; use concise Target and Constraint fields for other observable checks. Add Violation only when the failure response is part of the contract. Do not merely restate the requirement title. Prefix proposals with `* [PROPOSAL]` and unresolved criteria with `? [NEEDS_INPUT]`. Use `AC-xxx` identifiers only when stable references or independent tracking are useful.

children.title: User Journeys
children.guidance: Optional end-to-end scenarios. Include journeys when they clarify multi-step behavior that is not captured as well by individual requirements. Refer to requirements instead of restating their rules or acceptance criteria.

children.title: Journey: {name}
children.guidance: Replace {name} with a descriptive name for one meaningful journey. Each instance must contain a flow and preconditions.

children.title: Flow & Preconditions
children.guidance: Describe the trigger, starting conditions, and important sequence. Include relevant design references and links to requirements.

children.title: End-to-End Acceptance Criteria
children.guidance: Optional criteria owned by this end-to-end journey. Do not repeat requirement-level criteria.

children.title: Risks, Dependencies & Open Decisions
children.guidance: Optional delivery considerations. Include populated collections only. An unknown fact is not automatically a product decision; identify whether it needs verification or a choice.

children.title: Risks
children.guidance: Optional collection of material uncertain adverse outcomes and their mitigations or next actions.

children.title: Risk: {risk}
children.guidance: Describe the uncertainty, likely impact, and known mitigation or next action.

children.title: Dependencies
children.guidance: Optional collection of external inputs or conditions needed for delivery.

children.title: Dependency: {dependency}
children.guidance: Describe what is needed and any relevant condition, owner, or impact when known.

children.title: Open Decisions
children.guidance: Optional collection of consequential unresolved product choices. Include known options, evidence, trade-offs, and what depends on resolution.

children.title: Decision Needed: {question}
children.guidance: Replace {question} with the open question. Describe the choice, viable options, a recommendation when one is defensible, and what depends on the answer. Mark the unresolved behavior `? [NEEDS_INPUT]` rather than presenting it as settled.
